newsitem.title: FINLAND: OKOBANK SEES BULLISH GROWTH IN 1997 INVESTMENTS.
newsitem.headline: OKOBANK SEES BULLISH GROWTH IN 1997 INVESTMENTS.

text.p: Finnish investments will show brisk 14.5 percent growth in 1997 as the focus of investments will be shifting to the domestic market from the export industry, cooperative banking group OKOBANK said in its a forecast on Monday.

"The focus of growth is shifting from machine and equipment purchases to construction investments, and from the export industry to the domestic market," OKOBANK chief economist Matti Huomo told a news conference.
Housing investments are expected to increase 20 percent this year, he added.
According to preliminary data, housing investments fell 2.4 percent in 1996.
OKOBANK expects private sector investments to increase 15 percent and public investments 12 percent this year. It forecast 1997 GDP growth of five percent.
Construction and agricultural investments are also set to show firm growth in 1997, Huomo said, adding that the strongest building period for industry was over for now.
The cyclical pick-up in domestic market investments will reflect on employment as well, and the jobless rate could temporarily fall below the 13 percent level during some months of 1997, Huomo said.
OKOBANK's annual average jobless rate forecast for 1997 was 14.5 percent and 13 percent for 1998.
Employment would increase particularly in services and construction this year.
Credit demand is expected to show growth with banks' markka lending stock seen increasing four percent in 1997 and six percent in 1998, OKOBANK said.
Last year, banks' markka lending stock grew 2.6 percent.
